text:
olivia: Customer (Acme Mobile) escalated — streaming responses abort mid-message when the device switches from 5G -> corporate WiFi. They see a partial JSON chunk and then client shows EOF, no retry. Happening for ~20% of sessions, reproducible on a Pixel 6 with vendor carrier X.

ben: Ack. Do we have server logs or a sample client trace? Any 4xx/5xx on the gateway?

olivia: Pasted the minimal server log excerpt from the proxy: 
```
2026-02-14T08:12:22.123Z proxy INFO request_id=acme-req-987 path=/v1/streams model=gpt-4x size=560 token_count=120
2026-02-14T08:12:26.341Z proxy WARN request_id=acme-req-987 socket_close remote_addr=10.2.3.45 reason=client_eof code=499
2026-02-14T08:12:26.342Z runtime DEBUG request_id=acme-req-987 last_sent_chunk="{\"choices\":...partial..."
```
Client side log (from customer):
```
[2026-02-14 08:12:24] SSE: onmessage chunk received (partial)
[2026-02-14 08:12:25] Network: switched 5G -> WiFi
[2026-02-14 08:12:26] Connection closed unexpectedly, no close event
```

raj: 499 indicates client closed before finish. This looks like a device-level TCP teardown during NAT binding change. A few carriers tear down flows when IP changes. Could be NAT hole re-open delay.

ben: Is the client doing any reconnection/resume logic? Last-Event-ID or resume token?

olivia: Customer app does a one-shot SSE stream without resume. They expect the SDK to retry once transparently. They said retry didn't kick in because the client closed with EOF rather than a proper error.

eng-runtime: Noted. Two angles: (1) client-side keepalive/heartbeat to detect soft disconnect and trigger reconnect, (2) server-side resume token support or a short-lived caching buffer to allow resumption. We don't currently support Last-Event-ID resume for streaming API.

ben: Can we repro in-lab? Steps requested from eng to customer:
- Android Pixel 6 (Android 13)
- Open SSE stream to /v1/streams with user token
- While streaming, toggle mobile data off (or enable airplane briefly) then turn on WiFi to reproduce 5G->WiFi handoff
- Capture tcpdump on device and server side

olivia: Customer provided a repro script they used (adb based). Sharing truncated version: 
```bash
# open stream (client test app)
adb shell am start -n com.acme.stream/.MainActivity
# wait 6s then toggle mobile data off
adb shell svc data disable
sleep 2
adb shell svc wifi enable
# collect logs via logcat
adb logcat -d | grep "SSE" > /tmp/sse.log
```

raj: Helpful. Quick mitigations we can recommend to customer now: 1) enable client heartbeat every 10s and detect SOFT_CLOSE to trigger reconnect; 2) set HTTP keepalive options and TCP keepalive on sockets; 3) implement idempotent resume by checkpointing generated tokens and re-requesting with a resume cursor if duplicate responses tolerated.

olivia: Customer asked about server-side config — can we lengthen idle NAT time or change load-balancer timeouts? They saw socket_close at ~4s after last chunk.

eng-runtime: We can't change carrier NAT. On LB side we have keepalive defaults: idle timeout 60s. The 4s figure matches client side or OS killing socket during interface change. Server saw immediate FIN? Logs show client-originated close (no TCP RST from server).

ben: For triage, can eng-runtime add detailed connection tracing for a single customer session (enable pcap capture and verbose tcp/socket lifecycle logs) so we can correlate? We should also add a small instrumentation header to responses that the client can echo back when reconnecting (to help dedupe).

eng-runtime: We'll enable extra tracing for the next 24h on the customer's tenant for a small sample of requests. Assigning to @eng-runtime for capture.

infra-bot: Created trace capture job job_id=trace-175888-01 for tenant=acme-mobile window=24h.

olivia: Also flagged to the customer that their SDK should treat EOF as retriable for mid-stream and attempt a fast reconnect with a short exponential backoff. They agreed to patch and test.

raj: FYI — there is an older Chrome/Android WebView bug where socket.close during network change can produce no close frame for SSE. If the app uses WebView, recommend a native socket layer or upgrade WebView.

ben: Next steps checklist:
- eng-runtime: enable pcap + socket tracing (ETA 4h)
- support: request full device tcpdump + app logs (Olivia) (ETA 1d)
- customer: add client-side heartbeat + EOF->reconnect patch (ETA 2d)
- eng-product: evaluate short-term server resume prototype (internal spike) (ETA 1w)

olivia: I'll update the customer and file a formal incident if we see >10% failing on tracing window. For now logged as support escalation INC-2026-51.

support-bot: Escalation logged: INC-2026-51 | Priority: P2 | Owner: olivia | Link: https://support.redwood.ai/inc/INC-2026-51

ben: Thanks team. If anyone captures a reproducible packet-level trace, drop it here and we'll decide on a server-side mitigation. :thumbsup:

olivia: Will follow up after trace run finishes. Closing thread for now but will reopen with artifacts. :spiral_calendar:
